title: Champaign location page slipping a 3rd straight period: pos 6.1 -> 6.8, clicks -15% (286 -> 242)
detail: /locations/champaign-il is the only location page with a genuine, persistent ranking drift. Non-branded position has drifted three periods running (4.4 -> 6.1 -> 6.8) and clicks are now down -44 (-15%), crossing the flag threshold, with impressions -540. Branded intent is still healthy - 'forage kitchen champaign' is up (81 -> 108 clicks) and 'forage kitchen champaign menu' jumped to pos 1.6 (from 4.1) - so people searching the store by name still convert. The erosion is on the broader, non-branded local visibility that feeds the map pack and 'restaurants in champaign'-type discovery. Action: search 'forage kitchen champaign' and 'healthy food champaign il' from a Champaign IP and note who now outranks the page at 6-7; confirm the Champaign Google Business Profile is verified with current hours/photos/category and steady review velocity; refresh the page copy with campus/neighborhood terms (UIUC, Campustown, downtown Champaign) and verify complete LocalBusiness schema. This is the second period I have flagged Champaign - if position keeps sliding next week it warrants a technical crawl/index check on the page.

title: RESOLVED: Whitefish Bay and Pewaukee - both last week's HIGH ranking losses recovered
detail: Two wins to bank. (1) Whitefish Bay: the escalating loss on 'forage kitchen whitefish bay' reversed - position recovered to 1.4 (it was 2.2 last week, near-#1 again) and the /locations/whitefish-bay page is now a gainer (578 -> 604 clicks, pos 2.8). The variant 'forage whitefish bay' also surged +107 clicks with position improving 3.2 -> 2.0. The remaining exact-term click dip is query-variant reshuffle + demand, not a ranking problem. (2) Pewaukee: the three-week decline reversed - /locations/pewaukee flipped to +20 clicks (291 -> 311) and position improved 3.7 -> 3.3, and the branded query 'forage kitchen pewaukee' improved to pos 1.2. No action needed on either beyond routine monitoring; whatever GBP/local-slot pressure was in play has eased. Keeping this as a high-visibility note so the recovery is on record - if either regresses next week, re-escalate immediately.

title: /faq page dropped -95 clicks (-27%) with position 4.7 -> 5.1 - largest non-blog page decline
detail: The FAQ page was the single biggest non-blog page loser this period: 354 -> 259 clicks (-95) with position sliding 4.7 -> 5.1 and impressions -262. Because BOTH clicks and position fell, this is partly a ranking slip rather than pure demand. The FAQ page tends to capture 'is forage gluten free', 'forage nutrition/allergen' style questions - note 'forage kitchen nutrition' also fell (144 -> 72 clicks) this period. Action: confirm no recent title/H1 or content change regressed the page; verify it still carries FAQPage structured data (question/answer schema) so it is eligible for the rich result; make sure the highest-intent Q&As (allergens, gluten-free, nutrition, catering) are near the top and internally linked from /menu and the homepage. Recovering to pos ~4.5 is worth ~90 clicks/28d.

title: 'Near me' LocalBusiness schema audit still open - food near me improved (pos 11.8 -> 11.4) but salad/vegan/gluten-free near-me terms fell out
detail: Carried forward and partially improving. Bright spot: 'food near me' gained this period (108 -> 173 clicks, position improved 11.8 -> 11.4, 11.4k impressions), and the health-forward angle keeps working. But the softer near-me variants slipped or vanished: 'salad near me' -17 clicks (pos 8.2 -> 8.5), and 'vegan near me', 'gluten free food near me', and 'healthy food' all dropped to zero clicks this period. This is the still-unfinished task from prior weeks. Action: complete the schema audit - confirm every /locations/* page carries full LocalBusiness data (name, address, geo coordinates, opening hours, telephone, menu URL) plus an embedded Google map, and that each Google Business Profile category/hours/photos are current. Lean location and homepage copy toward 'healthy'/'fresh' near-me phrasing, the near-me angle Forage actually ranks best on.

title: Cobb-salad content cluster losing position across 4 pages - refresh candidate
detail: A cluster of salad content declined together this period, which usually signals a content-freshness or SERP-reshuffle issue rather than four independent problems. 'cobb salad' lost its ranking entirely (16 -> 0 clicks, was pos 2.7); /blogs/cobb-salad-a-healthy-choice -40 clicks (pos 4.8 -> 5.3); /blogs/cobb-salad-dressings -21 clicks with position dropping hard (6.0 -> 9.4); /blogs/salad-toppings -20 clicks (pos 11.8 -> 14.9). These are non-branded informational posts that pull top-of-funnel traffic. Action: refresh the two highest-value posts (cobb-salad-a-healthy-choice and cobb-salad-dressings) - update the publish date, tighten the intro to match current 'cobb salad' intent, add/refresh FAQ schema, and cross-link them plus link from /menu. Lower urgency than the location pages since it is top-of-funnel, but a cheap content refresh should recover most of the ~80 lost clicks.

title: Total impressions -32% again, still one blog post - demand/SERP, not a site-wide ranking loss
detail: Site impressions fell 1.10M -> 751k, and ~240k of that drop is again a single post: /blogs/fermented-food went from ~348k to 109k impressions while its position stayed flat (8.6 -> 8.6). Stable rank + collapsing impressions = a demand or SERP-feature pullback on a large informational query (likely absorbed by an AI overview), not lost rankings. The proof it is low-value: non-branded clicks actually ROSE this period (+49 to 1802) despite the impression collapse. Do NOT chase the impression number. If you want to defend non-branded over time, refresh the 2-3 highest-value informational posts (forbidden-rice, fermented-food, kale-vs-spinach): update publish dates, refresh FAQ schema, add homepage/menu internal links. Standing low-priority gap unchanged: /locations/state-street-madison-wi remains the weakest location page (56 clicks) despite strong Madison intent - add a prominent homepage link to State Street.
